quote.translation: When Plato, on the other hand, criticises the atomists by saying that "according to what they say, it seems that nature (φύσις) and chance (τύχη) made the greatest and most beautiful things, and art made the lesser" (Platon, Leges, X, 889), or "not through mind, nor through any god, nor through art, but through nature (φύσις) and chance (τύχη)" (Ib.), the chance he means is properly understood as teleological contingency in heterogeneous combination with the causal necessity called nature.

quote.translation: Leibniz distinguished, within chance, between contingence and hasard (Leibniz, Opera philosophica, ed. Erdmann, p. 763).

regions.text: mann,p763）°contingenceとは自由や自發性と一群をなすものとされてゐるから、目釣々必然と異種結合をしてるる即知脚側然と見て遊支ない。まれhasardは强制力や絶對的必然性と同題として取扱はれてゐるから因果的必然と異種結合をしておる旨脚知偶然と見てよい。現代にあつてもプートルーはライプニッツに徴って因果偶然をComfingcnceと云ひ、目的々個然をhasardと云ってるる。

quote.translation: Since contingence is treated as belonging to one group with freedom and spontaneity, there is no objection to regarding it as causal contingency in heterogeneous combination with teleological necessity; and since hasard is treated as of the same kind as compulsion and absolute necessity, it may be regarded as teleological contingency in heterogeneous combination with causal necessity.

quote.translation: In modern times Boutroux, following Leibniz, likewise calls causal contingency contingence and teleological contingency hasard.

regions.text: 例へば、自說に對する反對論者の立場に立つて因果偶然が目々偶然へ導かれはしないかとの疑問を揺げてゐる場合に『contingenceの原理はhasardでないとしたら、一體何であり得る♪（BSoutroux,Delacontingencedesloisdehanaturergeed,p140）を云つてある。

quote.translation: Where, for example, he takes the standpoint of the opponents of his own theory and raises the question whether causal contingency is not led into teleological contingency, he asks: "If the principle of contingence is not hasard, what in the world can it be?"

quote.translation: (Boutroux, De la contingence des lois de la nature, 9e éd., p. 140).

regions.text: またそれに對する答辯として「若しも決定的原因の系列のうらに或度までConingenceが支配しないとしたならば、目原因の系列のうちにhasardが支配するであらう」（BV）-7143）と云つてゐる。

quote.translation: And in reply he says: "If contingence did not to some degree reign in the series of determining causes, hasard would reign in the series of final causes" (Ib., p. 143).
